by.claim: rfc-001 moves the application-sync privilege boundary onto the destinationServiceAccounts-impersonated SA but never extends that boundary to the diff codepath, which still runs under the raw cluster Secret identity. T-28695 shows this gap forces external-cluster operators to keep broadening a single cluster-role's patch grant (five rounds and counting) as the only workaround, re-coupling exactly the control-plane/application-privilege split rfc-001 set out to decouple. Reversing it requires shipping diff-path impersonation and then a separate migration to walk back every already-granted resource kind on the standing credential.

The PRD locks the Reverse deletion strategy to the invariant that rollingSync.steps stays a strictly sequential, one-match-group-at-a-time list 'for as long as this feature exists,' but T-28755 proposes parallel step groups inside that same rollingSync.steps structure. Adopting parallel steps silently breaks the last-in-first-out ordering Reverse depends on; unwinding requires either excluding parallel groups from Reverse entirely or a coordinated redesign of the deletion strategy, needing agreement from both the deletion-strategy owners and whoever implements T-28755.

T-28927's maturity-review scope call freezes strategy.rollingSync.steps' matchExpressions-list shape as the backward-compatible v1 contract once Progressive Sync ships Stable. T-28755's parallel-steps proposal changes exactly that shape, so if Stable ships first, parallel steps can only land as a new coexisting field rather than an in-place restructuring. That locks in two permanent step-expression mechanisms; collapsing them back to one later requires a deprecation cycle across every existing rollingSync.steps consumer, gated by the same back-compat bar that froze the shape.

rfc-002's CommitManifests proto2 message marks repoURL, targetBranch, drySHA, commitAuthor, commitMessage, and commitTime as required, a wire commitment that can never be relaxed once shipped clients depend on it. T-27327's proposed rollback flow (checkout an old rendered tree and re-push) is exactly the second caller the RFC didn't design for: it isn't hydrating a fresh dry commit, yet must still populate all six required fields with values that don't map cleanly onto what it's doing. Undoing this coupling later needs a new message/RPC version, since the existing required fields can't be loosened for callers already built against them.

distractorGate.note: DX1/DX2 violations fail rung 3 for runs scored from this date; score files recorded earlier are never regenerated and keep their as-run results.
